newsitem.title: USA: Florida boy lived for two months in cave.
newsitem.headline: Florida boy lived for two months in cave.

text.p: For two months a homeless Florida teenager lived in an underground cave after slipping through the cracks of the social welfare system.
But Cliff Welty said Thursday that things were looking up. He has had offers of help since his story was printed in a local newpaper.
"I've had some job offers today," Welty told Reuters. "Some people are offering to take me in..."

When his father lost his job last December, Welty, then 16, went to live with his mother in Melbourne, Florida. But a long history of family problems continued to plague him and, two weeks later, his mother threw him out of her home.

Welty returned to Ocala but could not find his father. He was unable to stay in shelters or apply for social services because he was underage and could not check into a children's home because he was not in trouble or a runaway.
Welty said he began sleeping in a deep cave where he had once played with friends.

"It was lonely and cold," said Welty, now 17. "At first, it was just a place to spend the night until I could look for work. Then it was another night, and another night. Pretty soon I just didn't feel like there was any alternative."
When he looked for work, he could not supply an address or a phone number. He survived on odd jobs and by digging through waste bins behind fast-food restaurants.
Soon, his clothes were filthy and he had not bathed in two weeks, so the search for steady employment turned to panhandling and holding a "will work for food" sign.
"Who's going to hire someone whose pants are covered with two weeks of dirt and grease?" he said. "My job was trying to find a way to survive every day."

Patricia Miller, a local activist for the homeless, found a home for Welty and said there have been more than 200 offers of help. "We're just getting more and more of these kids falling through the cracks," she said.
